SMTO-K8S-0004 — SMTO couldn't use a saved Kubernetes cluster record

GUID: 4b1fe240-0ccc-4b28-87cf-777725489c0a
Slug: kubernetes-config-revision-invalid
Domain: K8S · Subsystem: k8s

What happened

  • SMTO keeps a short record of which Kubernetes cluster a conversation used. That record's check code or settings file location is missing or damaged, so SMTO set it aside. Your cluster and commands weren't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the agent to run a read-only command, such as kubectl get pods, on the cluster and namespace you want. A fresh successful command creates a new, valid record that replaces the unusable one.
  2. Make sure the conversation is using the same Gateway and Kubernetes settings file as when the cluster was first used. A cluster record only matches the Gateway and settings file it was made from.

What success looks like

  • The read-only command succeeds and later Kubernetes steps use the cluster you expect.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit SMTO's saved data files to repair the record.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Kubernetes setup validation rejected cluster_identity or config_revision values that are not 64-character SHA-256 hex digests, or a config_ref whose source is not default, environment or explicit, or whose path is empty, unsafe or not absolute.

What this means

  • Public setup validation rejects non-digest cluster/config revisions or a config_ref with invalid fields, source, path bounds or nonabsolute path. These are local configuration/observation checks, not proof of cluster reachability or command rollback. Optional observation failure cannot change the underlying command outcome; diagnostics perform no cluster operations.

Why this can happen

  • Public setup validation rejects non-digest cluster/config revisions or a config_ref with invalid fields, source, path bounds or nonabsolute path.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the saved public reference with a fresh observation from the intended Gateway.

How to fix it

  • Treat the record as stale: run a supported read-only kubectl command (for example kubectl get pods) through the same Gateway so it emits a fresh setup with current digests and an absolute config_ref. Do not hand-edit saved digests or reuse a revision from another setup.
  • Refresh supported Kubernetes discovery from the intended kubeconfig and use its returned public reference and revision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The public setup contains valid current digests and an exact supported native config reference.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • These are local configuration/observation checks, not proof of cluster reachability or command rollback. Optional observation failure cannot change the underlying command outcome; diagnostics perform no cluster operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
